title: Finite-field closed-support constructibility
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $A$ a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Let $Rg^!$ be the ambient right adjoint to exact closed direct image [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Then $Rg^!\mathcal B_A(T)\subseteq\mathcal B_A(Z)$. No global cohomological-dimension bound on $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, closed-immersion support-triangle proof, specialized to R=A and m=0.

proof.text: Let $j:U=T\setminus g(Z)\hookrightarrow T$ be the complementary open immersion. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is Noetherian and every open subset of $T$ is quasi-compact. Hence $j$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open of $T$ is an open subset of this Noetherian space. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] it is locally of finite type, hence finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Applying [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to $U\to T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $U$ finite type over $k$. Thus the support-triangle theorem applies to $(g,j)$, and the finite-field direct-image theorem applies to $j$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: For $h=j$ or $h=g$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies $h^{-1}A_T$ with the constant ring on its source. In [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], extension along this isomorphism merely identifies scalar actions. The underlying abelian inverse image is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]; kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have their induced scalar actions, so $h^*$ is exact as well. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^q(h^*K)\cong h^*\mathcal H^q(K)$ for every complex $K$ and integer $q$, with $h^*$ applied termwise on the ordinary derived category. In particular, pullback preserves the cohomological vanishing interval.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: The same pullbacks preserve constructible cohomology. For a finite stratification $T=\coprod T_a$ as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], put $S_a=S\times_TT_a$ ($S$ the source of $h$): its projection $i'_a$ to $S$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], and $h\circ i'_a=i_a\circ h_a$. The $S_a$ partition $S$ into finitely many locally closed subsets, constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. By [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition], $i_a'^*h^*F\cong h_a^*i_a^*F$, and [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] gives this a covering with the same finite $A$-module models, hence finite geometric stalks. Finite $A$-modules are finite-dimensional. With step 2, $h^*\mathcal B_A(T)\subseteq\mathcal B_A(S)$. Empty strata are discarded.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Fix $K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$. Step 3 gives $j^*K\in\mathcal B_A(U)$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-proetale-direct-image] to the finite-type map $j$ of step 1: $Rj_*j^*K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$. The field and coefficient hypotheses are exactly the ones in this item; that theorem does not assume a cohomological-dimension bound on $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: By [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle], in the ambient ordinary derived category there is a distinguished triangle $C\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to C[1]$, where $C=g_*Rg^!K$. Its exceptional inverse image is the right adjoint of the same closed direct image as in the statement; uniqueness of right adjoints identifies any choices. By [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated], $\mathcal B_A(T)$ is invariant under isomorphisms and shifts and is closed under triangle extensions. Rotate the triangle to $Rj_*j^*K[-1]\to C\to K\to Rj_*j^*K$. Its outer vertices lie in $\mathcal B_A(T)$ by step 4 and the hypothesis on $K$, so $C\in\mathcal B_A(T)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Apply $g^*$ to $C$. Step 3 gives $g^*C\in\mathcal B_A(Z)$. The counit $g^*g_*M\to M$ is an isomorphism for every module sheaf $M$ by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful], and $g_*$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], since its complementary open immersion is quasi-compact by step 1. Both functors therefore descend termwise to ordinary derived categories; applying the sheaf counit degree by degree to any representative of $Rg^!K$ yields $g^*g_*Rg^!K\cong Rg^!K$. Consequently $Rg^!K\in\mathcal B_A(Z)$ by the isomorphism invariance in [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. When $Z$ is empty the value is zero, and when $Z=T$ the same counit identifies the value with $K$; these include the boundary cases. No step uses finiteness of the absolute cohomological dimension of $k$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q69-1bdb269ee (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.11 (PDF p.56), specialised to R=A a finite field and m=0, plus all six steps and every cited statement. The item is true and unchanged from the base, and has no new nodes. Steps 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 match their citations. Step 1: Noetherianity and finite type give the hypotheses of the support triangle and of the direct-image node. Step 2: the constant-ring isomorphism makes h^* exact and commuting with cohomology. Step 4: lem-sfb-finite-field-proetale-direct-image is unsplit, has no CD bound and creates no cycle. Step 5: support triangle, rotated so lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated applies. Step 6: counit iso (closed-fully-faithful) plus closed-exact give g^*g_*Rg^!K = Rg^!K. Fault (C1/C3), fixed: step 3 used three facts it did not cite. It computed (h^*F) on S×_T T_a as h_a^*(F|T_a) without the composition of module pullbacks, justified constructibility of the preimage strata by an uncited 'Noetherian, hence constructible', and did not cite that the base-changed stratum inclusion is an immersion. FIX: step 3 now cites lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition, lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage and lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft(1), and states that geometric stalks are finite. proof_deps is recomputed and the two new off-unit tools are declared in tool_uses; I checked that neither creates a cycle. lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible is the BS 6.5.8 analogue but uses the sk-def-sfb module-object sense, so it was not substituted. Edge cases: Z empty, Z=T, k of infinite cd, nonreduced Z. No SGA cited.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

lean.statement: theorem finiteFieldClosedSupport_bounded_constructible (ℓ p : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] (_hp : 0 < p) (_hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ) (A : Type u) [Field A] [Finite A] [CharP A ℓ] {Z T : Scheme.{u}} [Z.Over (Spec (.of k))] [T.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of k))] (g : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion g] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory T A) (_hK : Set.Finite {q : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A)) q).obj K)} ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf T A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A)) q).obj K)) : Set.Finite {q : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules Z (proEtaleConstantRing Z A)) q).obj ((sfIntrinsicClosedUpperShriek g (Scheme.Opens.ι (⟨(Set.range g)ᶜ, g.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range.isOpen_compl⟩ : T.Opens)) A).rightDerivedFunctor.obj K))} ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Z A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules Z (proEtaleConstantRing Z A)) q).obj ((sfIntrinsicClosedUpperShriek g (Scheme.Opens.ι (⟨(Set.range g)ᶜ, g.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range.isOpen_compl⟩ : T.Opens)) A).rightDerivedFunctor.obj K))
